name: POST /api/leadflow/kpi-definitions/tiles - the ship gate
description:
Declares a dashboard tile, and REFUSES one whose metric is not registered (44fa2588-4db3-48f4-a653-2c0a970f94fc#AC1, 44fa2588-4db3-48f4-a653-2c0a970f94fc#AC4). This is the enforcement point: a tile cannot be declared, and therefore cannot ship, unless the metric it displays already exists in the registry. Putting the check here rather than in a lint rule means it also holds for tiles added at runtime, which a build-time gate cannot see at all.

A 422 rather than a 400 - the request is well formed and the intent is clear; what is missing is a precondition in the world. The refusal names the metric and what to do about it.

QA: measured live; a tile referencing an unregistered metric was refused, and the same call succeeded once the definition existed.

testCases.name: A tile referencing a registered definition is accepted
A tile whose metric is not in the registry is REFUSED
NEGATIVE: no Authorization header at all
NEGATIVE: a bearer token that does not verify

errorCases.message: dashboard_key, tile_key and metric_key are all required
errorCases.when: any of the three is absent.

errorCases.message: No registered KPI definition exists for "made_up_metric", so this tile cannot ship. Register the definition first - a tile whose meaning is written only in its own query is how two dashboards end up disagreeing.
errorCases.when: the metric key has no current registered definition.

errorCases.message: Authorization header with a bearer token is required
errorCases.when: the Authorization header is absent, empty, or uses a scheme other than Bearer.

errorCases.message: Session token is invalid or expired
errorCases.when: a Bearer token was presented but does not verify.
